record.paper_title: Frequently hypercyclic operators: recent advances and open problems
record.original_question: Which Banach spaces admit a frequently hypercyclic operator, meaning a continuous linear operator with an orbit that visits every nonempty open set with positive lower density? Which Banach spaces admit a chaotic operator, meaning a hypercyclic operator whose periodic points are dense?

evidence.quote:
Problem 4. Which Banach spaces admit a frequently hypercyclic operato r? Which Banach
spaces admit a chaotic operator?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a separable infinite-dimensional Banach space over the field K (where K = R or C). A continuous linear operator T : X → X is called:

(a) hypercyclic if there exists x ∈ X whose orbit {T^n x : n ≥ 0} is dense in X;
(b) frequently hypercyclic if there exists x ∈ X such that for every nonempty open set U ⊆ X, the set N(x,U) = {n ∈ N : T^n x ∈ U} has positive lower density, i.e.
  liminf_{N→∞} (1/N) #{n ≤ N : T^n x ∈ U} > 0;
(c) chaotic if T is hypercyclic and the set of periodic points {x ∈ X : T^p x = x for some p ≥ 1} is dense in X.

Characterize:
1. The class of separable infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X that admit a frequently hypercyclic continuous linear operator T : X → X.
2. The class of separable infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X that admit a chaotic continuous linear operator T : X → X.
artifact.status_search_result: The full characterization remains open. It is known that every complex separable infinite-dimensional Banach space with an unconditional Schauder decomposition admits a chaotic and frequently hypercyclic operator (de la Rosa–Frerick–Grivaux–Peris). On the other hand, there exists a real Banach space with an unconditional basis that admits no chaotic operator (Shkarin, Bonet–Martínez-Giménez–Peris-type constructions), and there are hereditarily indecomposable Banach spaces with no hypercyclic operators at all. No general intrinsic characterization of Banach spaces admitting frequently hypercyclic or chaotic operators is currently known.

status_evidence.title: Frequent hypercyclicity, chaos, and unconditional Schauder decompositions
status_evidence.snippet: If X is a complex separable infinite-dimensional Banach space with an unconditional Schauder decomposition, then X supports an operator T which is chaotic and frequently hypercyclic.
status_evidence.claim: Positive result on a large class of Banach spaces, but not a full characterization.

status_evidence.title: Linear Dynamical Systems (Gilmore survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys open problems on existence of frequently hypercyclic and chaotic operators on Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Existence/characterization problem remains an active open question.
